summaryPoints: England recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Jonny Bairstow's resolute 101 to post 307.
Stuart Broad's 6-wicket haul dismantled New Zealand for 278, handing the advantage to England.
A ruthless second-innings declaration at 352/9d by England established a massive 382 Runs target.
A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: New Zealand embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 382 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. Tom Latham anchored the innings with a resolute 83, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. MA Wood (2/45) maintained tight lines for England, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Dismissed for 256/8 (124.4 ov), New Zealand succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as England's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchStory: England recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Jonny Bairstow's resolute 101 to post 307. Stuart Broad's 6-wicket haul dismantled New Zealand for 278, handing the advantage to England. A ruthless second-innings declaration at 352/9d by England established a massive 382 Runs target. A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Hagley Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 307/10 (96.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 278/10 (93.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Tim Southee (6/61), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Tim Southee delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (50 Runs & 7 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 47%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by Colin Grandhomme (117 Runs & 4 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
